one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is the fiscal Q1 2027 (September quarter) report, expected around 2026-10-21. Guidance was revenue of $8.10B +/- $0.4B and EPS of $2.15 +/- $0.15. Lam has beaten recently (the June quarter beat by about $0.13), and brokers are raising their WFE forecasts, so a beat and a higher December-quarter guide are likely. Much of that is already expected: the stock is up about 29% since early August and trades about 34x FY27 consensus. Recent tape also shows AI-sector sell-offs hitting the name hard even after good prints (e.g. -5% on 2026-09-10 after record results). Other items in the window are peer prints (ASML and TSMC in mid-October) and possible China export-control headlines. I centre the distribution at about $326, a slight positive tilt from post-beat drift and momentum (the stock is above its 50-day and 200-day averages), with a lognormal sigma of 16.5% for the month. That is a little under the 65%/3.5 = 18.6% rule-of-thumb, because the realized-volatility figure includes the sharp drop from the June high, while the earnings gap widens the tails. The result is close to symmetric.

fair_value.method: The fair value is 55% forward P/E and 45% FCF yield, looking 12 months out. On P/E, estimated FY28 (June 2028) EPS of $12.0 times 26x gives $312. On FCF yield, estimated FY28 FCF of $12.6B at a 3.5% yield, plus about $1.9B of net cash, over 1.25B shares gives about $285. The blend is about $300, slightly below today's $324.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY2028 EPS $12.0 x 26x forward P/E (the stock is valued on NTM EPS in Sep 2027, i.e. FY28)

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus of $9.51 grown about 26%. This sits between JPMorgan's CY27-to-CY28 WFE growth (+16%) and Goldman's (+29%), plus some operating leverage toward management's mid-40s operating-margin target. It also assumes buybacks of about $4B a year shrink the share count by about 1%.

The current forward P/E is about 33x, and the 10-year median TTM P/E is about 20.7x. Semicap multiples usually compress as the cycle matures (WFE fell about 30% in 2019 and 20-25% in 2023). I haircut the current multiple toward the historical median but keep a premium for secular AI and DRAM growth still visible into 2028.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 revenue about $42B x 30% FCF margin = $12.6B FCF; 3.5% yield gives $360B; plus about $1.9B net cash; over 1.25B shares

inputs_detail.derivation: FY27 consensus of $34.9B plus about 20%, in line with broker WFE growth for 2027-28 (JPM $205B to $237B; GS $218B to $281B).

FY26 operating cash flow was $5.86B on $23.2B revenue (about 25%). The margin rises with the raised long-term framework (GM in the mid-50s, OM in the mid-40s) and with lower capex intensity at a higher scale.
The inverse of about 28x FCF, consistent with a mid-20s forward P/E for a high-conversion, late-upcycle business.
The filing shows 1.256B diluted shares, which matches the roughly $405B market cap at $324.

bear.story: By mid-2027 the market starts pricing a WFE digestion year for 2028: hyperscaler capex slows, DRAM pricing turns, or a US recession arrives (Polymarket prices about 35% by end-2027). China restrictions also tighten (Hua Hong curbs; China below 30% of revenue). FY28 EPS expectations fall to about $10 and the multiple drops to about 18-19x, near the historical median. That repeats the 40-55% semicap drawdowns of 2018, 2022 and 2024.

base.story: WFE grows to about $200B+ in 2027, led by DRAM and HBM, and Lam delivers FY27 EPS near $9.5 with FY28 visible at about $12. The multiple compresses from about 34x to about 27x forward as the cycle ages, so earnings growth and de-rating roughly offset. The stock ends near today's level.

bull.story: The Goldman-style supercycle plays out (WFE $218B in 2027 and $281B in 2028). Etch and deposition intensity in 3D DRAM, NAND upgrades and GAA/backside power give Lam share gains, and FY28 EPS reaches about $15. The market holds about 33x as it prices a longer cycle. The stock clears its June high of $438.50.

thesis_break_reason: About 22x FY27 consensus EPS and about 18x my FY28 estimate. A trade there would be roughly one-third below today and well under the 200-day average (~$299) and the post-earnings August base (~$252). That would mean the market has stopped believing in 2027-28 WFE growth, through a capex cut, a memory price rollover, a severe China export rule or a recession. Ordinary AI-sentiment volatility has so far held above about $250-265.

reasoning: Reported basics come from Lam's Q4 FY26 release: revenue of $23.2B for FY26 and $6.72B for the June quarter; a September-quarter guide of $8.1B and $2.15 EPS; CY26 WFE raised to the low $150Bs; and a higher long-term margin framework. Consensus FY27 EPS is $9.51 on $34.9B of revenue, and the average target is about $362-374. At $324 the stock trades about 34x FY27 and 51x TTM, versus a 10-year median of about 21x. My lane is base rates. First, semicap history says multiples compress as the cycle matures, even when earnings keep rising. WFE fell about 30% in 2019 and 20-25% in 2023, LRCX itself has had drawdowns of 40-55% in each recent cycle, and the stock already fell from $438.50 (June 30) to the $260s during September's AI sell-off. Second, the forward view is unusually strong: JPM and GS see WFE at $205-218B in 2027 and $237-281B in 2028, so earnings growth of about 25-30% a year into FY28 is plausible. Those two roughly offset, so my fair value is about $300 (26x on FY28 $12.0 EPS, plus FCF-yield cross-check). I put the median 12-month price near $318, slightly below spot, and the mean near $335 because of right skew. For dispersion I use a lognormal sigma of 0.50 rather than the 65% realized, which is inflated by the extreme 152% one-year move. That sits between a typical semicap's long-run 45-50% and the recent realized level. Macro base rate: Polymarket prices a 35% chance of a US recession by end-2027 (2026-09-24), which fattens the left tail. I reflect that in a bear case with 25% weight. The scenario mix (25% at $185, 50% at $325, 25% at $500) has a mean of about $334, consistent with the ladder.
